root_cause: PR #2053 was closed without merge after its branch diverged from current main. Reusing it would violate current-main and exact-head authority.
recovery: Reconstruct only the unique delivery-control-plane delta on current main; exclude stale Supabase migration copies and preserve all newer main learnings.
incident_findings: Parallel workers independently allocated the same Supabase migration timestamp, creating a global uniqueness failure despite locally valid changes.
Head-age based staleness would have cancelled healthy in-progress exact-head work and amplified queue thrash.
Multiple writers mutated one terminal delivery branch concurrently; non-force ref updates correctly prevented lost updates.
PR metadata can lag the authoritative Git ref during rapid concurrent recovery; exact branch ref is the source of candidate identity.
Duplicate PRs for one obligation create redundant CI fan-out and must be consolidated before terminal delivery.
prevention: Allocate final migration versions only at rolling-candidate integration and verify uniqueness before expensive CI.
Use per-run progress timestamps; never cancel healthy current-head in-progress work solely because the PR head is old.
Enforce one obligation-scoped terminal writer lease and fail closed on unexpected head mutation.
Use exact Git ref plus current main identity for recovery decisions; treat stale PR metadata as advisory.
Allow parallel specialists only for independent paths/contracts/resources; serialize the integration boundary, not all development.
Consolidate duplicate same-obligation PRs and supersede their CI instead of letting parallel release lineages accumulate.
